paragraphs.text: LXX gives the following introduction to vs 1: “And it occurred that, after Israel had been taken captive and Jerusalem had been desolated, Jeremiah sat down weeping and lamented with this lamentation over Jerusalem and said.” Vgmss introduce as follows: “And it occurred that, after Israel had been led away into captivity and Jerusalem was deserted, Jeremiah the prophet sat weeping and wailed with this lamentation over Jerusalem; and sighing with a bitter spirit, and moaning woefully, he said.” T introduces as follows: “Jeremiah the prophet and great priest said.”
“Into the congregation.” Heb., vaq·qa·halʹ; Gr., ek·kle·siʹan; Lat., ec·cleʹsi·am.
“Soul.” Heb., naʹphesh; Lat., aʹni·mam. See App 4A.
The Heb. word for “valueless” is fem. sing., as if a woman representing the city is speaking.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“They have heard,” MVg; T, “Nations have heard”; LXX, “Hear [pl.], please”; Sy, “Hear.”
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“All my people,” MLXXVg; Sy, “all peoples”; T, “all scatterers of my people.”
“Your,” emended by the Sopherim to read “my” in M; one of the Eighteen Emendations. See App 2B.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“Men.” Heb., ʼish, sing. but in a collective sense.
Or, “a living earthling man.” Heb., ʼa·dhamʹ chai.
Or, “O how the gold [Heb., za·havʹ] becomes dim, how the good gold [Heb., hak·keʹthem] changes!” See Job 28:16, 17 ftns.
“The productive land.” Heb., the·velʹ; LXX, “the inhabited earth”; Lat., orʹbis, “the circle,” that is, of the earth.
Or, “spirit (wind).” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus.
“Anointed one of.” Heb., meshiʹach; Gr., khri·stosʹ; Syr., meshi·cheh; Lat., chriʹstus.
“The cup,” MSyVg; T, “the cup of cursing”; LXX, “the cup of Jehovah.”
This chapter is not an alphabetic acrostic like each of the preceding four chapters, but it does have 22 vss to correspond to the 22 letters of the Heb. alphabet.
